name: correctness-go-channel-leak-no-close
description: Go producer goroutine that sends Events on a buffered channel but NEVER calls `close(out)` on any of its three exit paths (ctx.Done, io.EOF, decode error). The producer.go top docstring (lines 16–22) and the consumer.go docstring (lines 7–11) both explicitly state the channel-close-is-the-completion-signal contract; the consumer's `for ev := range events` loop depends on it. Net effect: when the producer exits normally on EOF, the 4 worker goroutines on consumer.go block forever waiting for the next event. Channel goroutine leak — invisible in unit tests that don't run with the race detector + leakcheck.

expected.description: The producer goroutine never closes `out`. All three exit paths (`<-ctx.Done`, decode-EOF, decode-error) `return` without `close(out)`. The contract documented on lines 16–22 of this file ('the channel is closed exactly when the producer is finished') is violated, and consumer.go's `for ev := range events` loop (line 28) depends on that close — it blocks forever after the producer exits. Result: 4 worker goroutines leak per call to `StreamEvents`. Fix: `defer close(out)` at the top of the goroutine body so every exit path closes correctly.

The new decode-error path (lines 42–44) silently swallows the error after a single Printf. The caller has no programmatic way to distinguish 'stream ended cleanly' from 'stream aborted on a malformed line' — both manifest as 'channel returned, no more events'. Should propagate via an error channel or via a sentinel Event with an error field that the consumer can react to.

`fmt.Printf` to stdout for a decode error is unstructured logging that the central logger never sees. The rest of the codebase uses `slog`/`zerolog`/`zap` (pick one); this single Printf is now an outlier the SIEM grep won't catch.
